models.strictJsonSchema: Partial, and it depends on the runtime (see notes). Ollama 0.40.7 /v1/responses maps text.format json_schema to a llama.cpp GBNF grammar. That grammar enforces: const and enum (strings and numbers); anyOf, including nested; type null and type arrays; integer minimum/maximum; additionalProperties:false. It silently ignores: minimum/maximum on type number; 'nullable'; the strict flag; any sibling keys next to anyOf/oneOf. llama-server /v1/responses ignores text.format entirely, so output is unconstrained there. llama-server Chat Completions response_format json_schema is honoured.

notes: SCOPE AND METHOD. I re-verified this research on 2026-10-21 from official docs, source code at pinned tags (read through raw.githubusercontent.com), Hugging Face API metadata, and GitHub discussion pages. The scratchpad holds earlier notes only for hosted providers (anth/, gem/, mistral/); I found no earlier local-inference notes to diff against, so everything below was checked fresh. Per-token prices are null for every entry because inference is local.

RUNTIME: Ollama v0.40.7. This is the 'Latest' stable release (18 Oct 2026); v0.40.8 is a pre-release from 21 Oct (https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases, read 2026-10-21). It runs natively on Windows.
(1) /v1/responses exists. The docs say 'Added in Ollama v0.13.3' and only stateless requests are supported (docs/api/openai-compatibility.mdx). At the v0.40.7 tag, openai/responses.go lines 868-876 map text.format {type:'json_schema', schema} to the chat 'format'. The 'strict' and 'name' fields are parsed but never used. Chat Completions response_format json_schema is mapped the same way (openai/openai.go).
(2) Enforcement is grammar-constrained. At v0.40.7, Ollama runs llama.cpp's llama-server as a subprocess (llm/llama_server.go). It sends the schema to llama-server's own json_schema-to-GBNF converter, and the bundled build is LLAMA_CPP_VERSION=b11738. I diffed common/json-schema.cpp, common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp and grammars/README.md: they are byte-identical between b11738 and b11799, so the keyword behaviour in the llama.cpp note below applies. Thinking stays unconstrained and the grammar starts after it closes (llm/llama_server.go header comment).
(3) Failure modes:
- On <24 GiB VRAM the default context is 4k (docs/context-length.mdx). chatPrompt in server/prompt.go silently truncates messages that exceed num_ctx, so a 9k-token observation is cut unless OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is at least 16384 or the Modelfile sets num_ctx.
- The Responses 'truncation' field is only echoed back. It is not mapped to the request, so the project's truncation:'disabled' is NOT honoured.
- 'seed' is not among the supported /v1/responses fields; it can be set in a Modelfile.
- tool_choice is unsupported (a TODO in the source).
- cache_prompt is hard-coded true (llm/llama_server.go line 1691).

RUNTIME: llama.cpp llama-server b11799 (commit 0756e83fc1529e207af783782905bc98a8ef0770, released 21 Oct 2026). Native Windows CUDA builds exist: llama-b11799-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip and -cuda-13.4-x64.zip, each with a matching cudart zip. MIT licence.
(1) POST /v1/responses exists. The README says it 'works by converting Responses request into Chat Completions request'. The converter, server_chat_convert_responses_to_chatcmpl in tools/server/server-chat.cpp, maps input, instructions, tools, max_output_tokens and reasoning.effort. It does NOT map text.format. The chat parameter parser in server-common.cpp only reads 'response_format' and top-level 'json_schema'. Result: text.format is SILENTLY IGNORED and output is UNCONSTRAINED. The current transport, pointed at llama-server /v1/responses, would therefore lose schema enforcement without any error.
(2) Chat Completions response_format {type:'json_schema', json_schema:{schema}} IS honoured, as is {type:'json_object', schema}; see server-common.cpp lines 1379-1392.
(3) The converter copies every top-level key into the chat body. Adding a top-level 'response_format' or 'json_schema' to a Responses body should therefore be honoured. That is my inference from the source; it is UNTESTED.
(4) It rejects previous_response_id.
All of this was read at tag b11799, and the files match master.

llama.cpp JSON Schema to GBNF behaviour, from source at b11799 (common/json-schema.cpp, common/json-schema-to-grammar.cpp, grammars/README.md). These are the keywords that matter for this schema:
- 'const' works for any JSON value, string AND number. It is emitted as a literal and takes precedence over 'type'.
- 'enum' works for any JSON values. 64-hex and 16-hex string enums are fine.
- anyOf works. oneOf is treated as anyOf, with no exclusivity. Nested anyOf works.
- When anyOf/oneOf is present, the node becomes ONLY the alternatives. Sibling 'properties' or 'type' on the same node are dropped; the README says 'Can't mix properties w/ anyOf/oneOf'.
- Type arrays such as ['string','null'] become anyOf. type 'null' is supported.
- OpenAPI 'nullable' is not recognised and is silently ignored.
- integer minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum are enforced. On type 'number' they are SILENTLY IGNORED.
- additionalProperties defaults to false, which is stricter than the spec. 'false' is enforced.
- Other unsupported keywords are skipped silently: uniqueItems, contains, not, if/then/else, patternProperties, prefixItems (broken), nested $ref (broken).
- An invalid pattern or an unresolved $ref throws 'JSON schema conversion failed' and the request is rejected.
- The schema is not injected into the prompt. This project already includes it in the input.
- A build with LLAMA_LLGUIDANCE uses llguidance instead. llguidance raises an error on unsupported keywords unless it is run in lenient mode (guidance-ai/llguidance docs/json_schema.md).
The project's schema checker (src/agent/responsesRequest.ts) requires additionalProperties:false and all properties required, and it uses enum, const and anyOf. Check whether any anyOf node also carries 'properties' or 'type'. Also check for number bounds or 'nullable'. Those are the constructs that would be silently weakened.

RUNTIME: LM Studio 0.4.26 (build 5), the newest entry at https://lmstudio.ai/changelog/lmstudio, read 2026-10-21. Build 2 bundles the 'llama.cpp runtime 2.50.0 (upstream b11337)'. It is closed source under proprietary terms (https://lmstudio.ai/app-terms) and runs natively on Windows.
- /v1/responses is documented: streaming, reasoning, previous_response_id, remote MCP. The page does NOT mention text.format.
- Structured output is documented only for /v1/chat/completions response_format json_schema. GGUF models use 'llama.cpp's grammar-based sampling APIs' and MLX models use Outlines (https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat/structured-output).
- Whether /v1/responses honours text.format, and keyword-level behaviour, are UNVERIFIED. Test before use.

RUNTIME: vLLM 0.32.0 (PyPI upload 2026-10-18).
- It does NOT support Windows natively. Its docs say to use WSL2 or a community fork (docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.md).
- /v1/responses honours text.format: vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py extract_structured_outputs maps json_schema to StructuredOutputsParams(json=schema). 'strict' is not used.
- Enforcement is token-mask constrained through xgrammar or llguidance. The default 'auto' tries xgrammar and falls back to guidance when the schema uses features xgrammar does not support (vllm/sampling_params.py). An explicitly chosen backend has no fallback.
- Structured outputs are not applied inside reasoning unless --structured-outputs-config.enable_in_reasoning=True is set.
- Reproducibility is not guaranteed by default. Online serving needs batch invariance, which is beta, requires NVIDIA compute capability 8.0 or higher, and only holds on the same hardware and version (docs/usage/reproducibility.md, docs/features/batch_invariance.md).
- I did not check how vLLM fits 16 GB under WSL2 for these models, or how fast it runs. I would not use it first on this PC.
- Other runtimes (SGLang, TabbyAPI/ExLlama) were NOT assessed.

- Meta: the HF org shows nothing newer than Llama 4 (Apr 2025), which I did not assess. The newest small model is Llama-3.1-8B (Jul 2024; gated, Llama 3.1 licence). Skipped as stale.

THROUGHPUT ANCHORS. These are the only measured numbers; every per-model figure is a labelled ESTIMATE scaled from them.
(a) llama.cpp CUDA scoreboard (github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/15013): RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, Llama-2-7B Q4_0, -fa 1, gave pp512 7,612 t/s and tg128 132.9 t/s (build 9c35706). The RTX 4080 SUPER gave 9,439 and 147.5.
(b) gpt-oss guide (discussions/15396): RTX 4080 SUPER, gpt-oss-20b MXFP4, gave pp8192 7,989, pp16384 7,518 and tg128 186.5 t/s (build 009b709). No 4070 Ti SUPER entry exists there.
(c) LocalScore, which runs on llamafile, so its numbers are conservative (localscore.ai/model/1 and /model/2): RTX 4070 Ti SUPER gave 3,561 t/s prompt and 53.9 t/s generation on Llama-3.1-8B Q4_K_M, and 2,147 and 36.8 on Qwen2.5-14B Q4_K_M.
Estimated time for a 9,000-token prefill plus 300 output tokens, thinking off, one request at a time:
- gpt-oss-20b: about 3-7 s, including low-effort reasoning.
- Ministral-3-8B Q4_K_M: about 4.5-8 s.
- Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M: about 5-9 s.
- Gemma-4-12B QAT Q4_0: about 6-10 s.
- Ministral-3-14B Q4_K_M: about 7-12 s.
All are within 16 s, but the margin narrows if a model emits reasoning tokens.
Measure before committing: llama-bench -m <file.gguf> -ngl 99 -fa 1 -p 9000 -n 300 -r 3. Then time a real request end-to-end, because grammar sampling adds overhead.
Volumes: the 630 calls of study 1 at about 5-10 s each come to roughly 1-2 h sequential. 3,000-4,000 calls come to about 4-11 h.

RESEARCH SUITABILITY: determinism.
- In llama.cpp, temperature <= 0 is argmax: src/llama-sampler.cpp line 270 at b11799 'find the token with the highest logit'. The seed is irrelevant at temperature 0. The default seed is -1, which means random.
- The llama-server README warns that cache_prompt (on by default) 'can cause nondeterministic results' because logits are 'not guaranteed to be bit-for-bit identical for different batch sizes'.
- For repeatable runs on the same PC, use llama-server with -np 1, cache_prompt:false (or --no-cache-prompt), temperature 0, and a fixed build, driver and settings. Turning the cache off costs one full prefill per call, which is still estimated at a few seconds.
- Ollama hard-codes cache_prompt:true and cannot expose this, so bitwise repeatability is not guaranteed there.
- vLLM needs batch invariance, which is beta.
- Treat repeatability as something to measure: rerun a fixed set of requests and diff the outputs and their sha256.

RESEARCH SUITABILITY: licences.
- gpt-oss-20b: Apache-2.0, plus a USAGE_POLICY file ('comply with all applicable law').
- Qwen3.5-9B: Apache-2.0.
- Gemma 4 (12B and 26B-A4B): Apache-2.0. The Gemma 4 licence page shows the Apache License 2.0 text, last updated 2026-04-01; its sidebar also links separate 'Prohibited use' and 'Terms of use' pages whose contents I did not read.
- Ministral 3 (8B, 14B): Apache-2.0.
- Runtimes: llama.cpp is MIT, Ollama is MIT, vLLM is Apache-2.0, and LM Studio is proprietary.
None of these model licences restricts research use as far as their stated licence goes.

RECOMMENDATION.
- Lowest-effort path with a verified schema guarantee: Ollama v0.40.7 /v1/responses. The existing Responses transport works with it, and text.format becomes a llama.cpp grammar. You MUST set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384 (or a Modelfile num_ctx), because 'truncation' is not honoured and overflow truncates silently. Accept that prompt caching cannot be turned off, so determinism is weaker.
- Most controllable path for research: llama-server b11799 with a small new adapter to /v1/chat/completions and response_format json_schema, or, untested, a top-level response_format added to the Responses body. Do NOT rely on llama-server /v1/responses text.format: it is ignored.
- Model order to test: gpt-oss-20b (closest to the current gpt-5.4-nano setup: reasoning effort 'low', Apache-2.0, fits with headroom), then Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma-4-12B with thinking off, then Ministral-3-14B.
- Whatever the runtime, validate every output against the schema client-side. Grammar enforcement silently drops some keywords: number bounds, 'nullable', and properties next to anyOf.
